title: OFF builds: dev vs base, kernel R0-R4 (Agent 11), IO cvars (Agent 12). Title/attract loop, no input needed
notes: All arms run the title/attract loop that the game reaches with no input, so the user can leave the PC alone (do not touch it while it runs).
The runner always passes --audio_mute=true --pause_when_unfocused=false --native_settings_load=false --discord_rpc=false (Get-GameArgs), as Agent 11 and Agent 12 ask.
The toml keeps the installer defaults, including framerate_limit = 60. A CPU-side win can then show as lower cpu_cores and fewer >33/>100 ms frames rather than a lower median.

Group 'off': deltas against r0 (devoff1-bin defaults). 'base' shows what the batch-1 dev changes do at defaults; r1..r4 are Agent 11's cumulative kernel cvars (r4 includes guest_suspend_guard), r0g is guest_suspend_guard alone; io-b is Agent 12's five cvars at the title (their level-load route is in matrix-io-level.json).
Agent 11's test G is a functional check and is NOT here: Agent 11 runs it from an agent command (agent11-kernel.md, 'Test G driver').
R1 check: game.log must show 'Host timer resolution set to 1 ms (background opt-out on)' in every r1..r4 run.

arms.note: dev OFF build 1 (S1), defaults; reference for the group
Agent 11 R1: 1 ms host timer + background throttling opt-out
Agent 11 R2 = R1 + precise guest sleep + wait timeout round-up
Agent 11 R3 = R2 + cs_spin, spinlock_pause_spin, clock_lockfree, tls_bounds_fix
Agent 11 R4 = R3 + object_lookup_fast_path + guest_suspend_guard (test G half 2, B ON, passed at 21:38)
Agent 12 arm B at the title loop (boot time and frame stats; the IO counters and the level-load route are in matrix-io-level.json)
Agent 11: R0 + guest_suspend_guard alone, to measure its cost. Lowest priority: leave it out with -Only if time is short
